items.statement: The submission uses one common, explicitly defined INT1-like reference ensemble and reports candidate provenance, deduplication, frequency validation, path validation, and a balanced free-energy convention for both O_site and C_site.
items.expected: Both channel records identify the same reference definition and provide individual frequency/path evidence; search coverage and stopping are documented.

items.statement: The retained O_site and C_site structures are validated as the requested stationary points and their path displacement involves the specified forming and breaking bonds.
items.expected: Each retained minimum has zero imaginary frequencies; each retained transition state has one relevant imaginary mode and IRC or equivalent endpoint confirmation, with atom-map connectivity 27-6/6-7 or 23-6/6-7 respectively.

items.statement: The authored INT1-relative solution barriers are 20.0 kcal/mol for O-site TS1 and 11.3 kcal/mol for C-site TS2.
items.expected: The report gives O_site near 20.0 kcal/mol and C_site near 11.3 kcal/mol, or transparently bounded failure with no fabricated numeric values.

items.statement: The authored transition-state structural descriptors distinguish TS1 and TS2: TS1 has N-S 2.32 Å and O-S 1.86 Å; TS2 has N-S 1.95 Å and C-S 2.33 Å.
items.expected: The submitted structural analysis reports these channel-specific trends or a method-qualified equivalent.

items.statement: The authors attribute the lower C-site barrier to stronger Na-pi and pi-pi interactions, while NPA charges do not account for the ordering.
items.expected: The mechanistic analysis separates charge observations from the interaction-based explanation and does not claim the charges alone cause selectivity.
